title: RC low-pass filter with f_c = 1 kHz
caption: With C = 100 nF the cutoff frequency f_c = 1/(2πRC) = 1 kHz needs R = 1/(2π × 1000 × 10⁻⁷) = 1.59 kΩ ≈ 1.6 kΩ. The output fraction |V_out/V_in| = 1/√(1 + (f/f_c)²) is 0.707 (−3 dB) at f = f_c, close to 1 well below it and about f_c/f above it.
alt: Graph of output over input amplitude against frequency over cutoff frequency: it starts at 1, falls through 0.707 at 1 and keeps falling.
description: The horizontal axis is f/f_c; the vertical axis is the amplitude ratio |V_out/V_in|.
At low frequency the capacitor passes nothing, so the output equals the input (ratio 1).
At f = f_c the ratio is 1/√2 = 0.707, the −3 dB point; R = 1.59 kΩ for C = 100 nF.
At high frequency the ratio falls as f_c/f: high frequencies are blocked.
